c.tagline: City of dreaming spires, centuries of scholarship, and cobbled college quads

taxi.fareNote: Licensed black cabs can be hailed on the street or found at ranks; minicabs are cheaper but must be pre-booked by phone or app

emergency.note: Dial 999 for emergencies (police, ambulance, fire); call 111 for non-urgent medical advice via the NHS

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Bike theft is rife, and Cornmarket Street and the station area see occasional pickpocketing and phone snatching.

hood_desc: Home to the historic university colleges, the Bodleian Library, and Radcliffe Camera. Pedestrianized streets and the Covered Market make it easy to explore on foot, though it gets crowded with tourists and students alike.
A charming Victorian-era neighborhood of terraced houses along the Oxford Canal, known for indie cafes, the Phoenix Picturehouse cinema, and a bohemian, arty feel.
A diverse, lively area southeast of the centre with some of Oxford's best curry houses, live music venues, and student-friendly bars along Cowley Road.
An affluent residential suburb north of the centre with boutique shops, delis, and a village-like high street popular with families.
A hillside suburb east of the centre, home to the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford Brookes University, and the famous fibreglass Headington Shark sculpture.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Roughly 5:30am-midnight, reduced service late night and Sundays
transit.pay: Contactless card, mobile app, or cash on board
transit.note: Oxford has no metro or tram; buses, walking, and cycling are the main ways to get around, along with Park & Ride from the edge of the city

train: Direct trains to London Paddington (~1 hour)
Direct trains to Birmingham, Reading, and Manchester
bus: Oxford Tube and National Express 24-hour coach services to London

tip.r: Restaurants often add a 10-12.5% service charge; if not included, 10% is appreciated. Not customary for taxis or pubs beyond rounding up
